tfa-cli.label: TODOforAI
tfa-cli.summary: Create and follow up on your TODOs, and show results in the chat.
tfa-cli.description: Manage the user's OWN TODOforAI tasks (not code `// TODO` comments). Delegate/spin off work: `tfa-cli "prompt"` creates a real TODO with its own agent and chat (`-n` wait for completion, `--no-watch` fire-and-forget, `--project/--agent/--model`, `--resume <id>`, `addmessage <id> "text"`). Inspect: `list [--status open]` (your own todos; `--project-wide` for every member's), `--inspect <id>`. Edit any todo without opening it: `status <id> DONE|READY|ARCHIVED|POSTPONED|CANCELLED|DELETED` (close, reopen, shelve, trash — `todo restore <id>` undoes a delete) and `todo set <id|-> title=… group=… star=true schedule=<unix-ms> agent=… brand=…` (own todo fields). Both take ONE id, so a loop over `list --json | jq -r '.items[].id'` is how you close, retitle, refile or archive MANY todos at once; `project set|settings|groups …` (name, settings, todo groups), `agent create|update <agent> model=… sysmsg=…` (also permissions=… and judgeSysmsg=…; MCP/device wiring and delete are refused from an agent shell). Surface results into chat: `show <file|-> [todo-id]` (renders by mimetype, private to the todo's readers; `--card <name>` via project renderer; `--alias <name>` updates in place, `show ref <alias|todoId:alias>` re-posts it live at the chat bottom, `--alias <todoId>:<name>` updates another todo's artifact; `show share <ref>` makes it public and prints the link, `show unshare <ref>` makes it private again), `open <url>` embeds a live preview. Show viewer chrome: `--title` appears in the header; a kebab menu holds file actions, versions and sharing when available. Desktop floating previews add minimize (park in a tab), maximize/restore and close (X); inline blocks have no window controls. For authored HTML, do not duplicate the header/controls or add a rounded, bordered root card: the floating viewer owns the rounded frame. Keep content edge-to-edge; internal layout padding is fine. Pick by where the output lives: read once → plain reply; interactive, this chat only → `html_snippet`; kept/revised later → `show --alias`, then `show share` only if someone outside needs a link; format the user asked for (pptx, docx…) → `show` the file. Notifications: `inbox [needs-you|messages|activity] [--unread]` reads the user's bell feed (what finished/failed/needs them while away), `inbox seen [tab]` marks it read; `notify "Title" "message" [--href /t/<id>] [--url <link>: tap opens it on the phone, e.g. a Google Maps navigation link]` leaves a note in the user's Messages tab + phone push (shown as from you); `--to <email>` reaches a member of the current project instead (`project members` lists them, 20/day) — nobody else; same text is delivered once, max 10/day to the user, use for things they must see later (not chat replies). This is the ONLY way to display a local file (image, pdf, html) in the chat: markdown `![](path.png)` with a local/relative path does NOT resolve to workspace files or attachments and 404s in the browser. `--template` for registry workflows. Project files: `memory sync|path [--project <id>]` requires a project and checks out only projects/<id>/{memory,context} and projects/<id>/me/{memory,context}; legacy global files are read-only recovery. Voice commands use `--scope mine|project` (default mine, private within this project; project is shared).

pymupdf.label: PDF
pymupdf.summary: Read, edit, merge and split PDF files.
pymupdf.versionCmd: { python -c 'import pymupdf; print(pymupdf.__version__)' || python3 -c 'import pymupdf; print(pymupdf.__version__)' || py -c 'import pymupdf; print(pymupdf.__version__)'; } 2>/dev/null
pymupdf.description: PDF read/edit/create via `python3 -c 'import pymupdf ...'`: text `doc[i].get_text()`, page count `doc.page_count`, page→PNG `page.get_pixmap(dpi=150).save()`, merge `a.insert_pdf(b)`, extract pages `doc.select([0,2])`, text/image→PDF `page.insert_textbox()` / `pymupdf.open("pdf", pymupdf.open(png).convert_to_pdf())`, stamp `page.insert_text()` / `page.insert_image(rect, filename=)`. HTML/URL→PDF: `chrome --headless=new --no-pdf-header-footer --print-to-pdf=out.pdf <url>`.

pyhanko.label: PDF Signing
pyhanko.summary: Digitally sign and verify PDFs with a certificate (PAdES, timestamps, smart cards).
pyhanko.description: Cryptographic PDF signing/validation (PAdES B-B..B-LTA). Sign: `pyhanko sign addsig --field Sig1 [--timestamp-url <tsa>] pkcs12 --passfile pass.txt in.pdf out.pdf cert.p12`; smart card/eID: `... pkcs11 --lib <pkcs11.so> in.pdf out.pdf`; verify: `pyhanko sign validate --pretty-print [--trust ca.pem] out.pdf`; list fields: `pyhanko sign list`. The signer's cert/key comes from the user (vault); self-signed certs validate only with `--trust`. Not for click-to-sign workflows.

anydoc.label: Doc to Markdown
anydoc.summary: Turn Word, PowerPoint, Excel and other documents into clean text.
anydoc.description: Office/rich docs (docx/pptx/xlsx/odt/rtf/epub/csv) → Markdown, fully local. `anydoc file.docx` → stdout, `-o out.md` writes, `anydoc - --format csv < stdin`. Prefer over raw XML extraction for reading; one-way, no OCR for scanned PDFs.

agent-browser.label: Browser
agent-browser.summary: Browse websites automatically: click, type, read and screenshot.
agent-browser.description: Browser automation over CDP (`open`/`snapshot`/`click`/`type`/`fill`/`read`/`screenshot`/`eval`). `connect '<url>'` to a listed live browser (prefer the user's real Chrome); connect prints `whoami` (browser=extension|embedded|local, headless, ua) — run `agent-browser whoami` again after any error or odd output, and stop on `ERROR`/`DISCONNECTED`/`headless=yes` where the user's browser was expected: re-run the connect command, never continue in another browser. If a page is empty, `close` (own session only) and reconnect once. NEVER `close --all`. Shared browser: `tab new` for your own tab, `tab <id>` before each command. No URL listed: cloud → browser-manager-cli; PC with display → Chrome `--remote-debugging-port=9222`, attach `--cdp 9222`. Never `sleep`: `open` returns after load, but `click`/`fill` fail at once if the element isn't there yet — `wait '<sel>'`, `wait --text 'Done'`, `wait --url '**/dash'`, `wait --load networkidle` or `wait '#spinner' --state hidden` first. Extension browsers (WEB_EXTENSION) only: try sign-in with credentials from `tfa-vault`; request human help only for a step you cannot complete yourself (MFA/CAPTCHA/consent). Use Node/Bun WebSocket on the listed CDP URL; `Target.getTargets` or `device_list` gives `tab-N`, whose N is the numeric tabId. On the SAME socket send `{id: 1, method: 'TodoforAI.requestHumanHelp', params: {tabId: N, message: 'what to do'}}` (message 1–500 chars). This only marks the tab (yellow count badge on the extension icon, needs-you row with Show in the popup); it never pauses you or takes the tab away. Tell the user what to do and to reply here, then end your turn. When resumed, snapshot to verify, then clear the marker with `TodoforAI.clearHumanHelp` `{tabId: N}`. If bootstrap fails on a restricted target, direct CDP `Target.createTarget` with an ordinary URL opens your tab on the SAME socket; pass numeric N from returned `tab-N` as `tabId`.

browser-manager-cli.label: Browser Manager
browser-manager-cli.summary: Start browsers in the cloud for automated browsing.
browser-manager-cli.description: Spawns cloud Chromium sessions, each exposed as a CDP WebSocket for agent-browser to drive. `create` prints one line ending in a cdpUrl — pass it straight to `agent-browser connect '<cdpUrl>'` (connect the cdpUrl, not the Chrome debug port). `list`/`get <id>`, `delete <id>`/`delete-all`, `hibernate`/`restore`. Sessions run stealth Chromium that reads as a real desktop browser. For sites that block datacenter IPs, route through a proxy: `create --proxy socks5://host:port [--proxy-user U --proxy-pass P]`. Use this on the cloud VM instead of launching a local browser.

tfa-explore.label: Explore
tfa-explore.summary: Send a helper agent to explore a codebase and report back.
tfa-explore.description: Sub-agent codebase exploration in its own context, you get only the answer: `tfa-explore "where is auth handled?" [--repo <path>]`. Prefer over manual multi-file searching.

tfa-review.label: Review
tfa-review.summary: Send a helper agent to review your code changes.
tfa-review.description: Sub-agent review of a git diff in its own context: `tfa-review "<goal>" [--repo <path>] [--against <ref>]` (default: uncommitted). Run before calling a non-trivial change done.

tfa-summary.label: Summary
tfa-summary.summary: Summarize files or long output with a helper agent.
tfa-summary.description: Sub-agent summary so raw text never enters your context: `cat big.log | tfa-summary "what failed?"`, or `-f <file>` (repeatable).

tfa-cat.label: Cat
tfa-cat.summary: Show images and PDFs from the shell to the agent.
tfa-cat.description: `cat` that lets you SEE media: `tfa-cat shot.png` (or `… | tfa-cat`) attaches images/PDFs to this bash result; text prints like cat; its stdout redirected/piped → raw bytes. Also `todoforai:<path>` files (`tfa-cat todoforai:todos/<id>/data.csv > data.csv`; binaries like docx/xlsx: redirect, then edit with your tools). Big text costs context: read what you need (`| head`, `| sed -n 40,80p`, `| grep -n`).

tfa-handoff.label: Handoff
tfa-handoff.summary: Turn a long conversation into a short handover note.
tfa-handoff.description: Compact a conversation into a handoff document for a fresh agent.

tfa-wait.label: Wait
tfa-wait.summary: Wait for a time or an event, then continue the task.
tfa-wait.description: Schedule a wake-up: `tfa-wait '<expr>' "<message>"` — expr is a time (`3h`, `daily@9:00`), a webhook, or a command's output; the message arrives later as a new chat message. Wait for a long job: `tfa-wait 'bench || 6h' "Done: exit {{payload.exit}}"` then `tfa-wait run '<cmd>' --pipe bench --on-exit &` (each stdout line = event; cancelling kills the command). Never pgrep/sleep poll loops. Standing automation ("when X happens, do Y" — survives this chat, shown under the agent's Automations): first test a check command that prints the FULL current list, one JSON line per item with a stable id, then `tfa-wait <word> --repeat --forever --new-todo --name "<label>" --watch '<check>' --every 5m "<what to do with {{payload.x}}>"` — the server runs it on this machine, fires only on new items; a failing check shows red in `tfa-wait list` and the UI.

tfa-cloud.label: TODOforAI Cloud
tfa-cloud.summary: Your TODOforAI cloud files from this computer: attachments, memory and brand page.
tfa-cloud.description: ssh host alias: `ssh tfa-cloud 'command'`, `scp`/`rsync` for files. Same root account, files, tools and logins as the cloud's own bash tool; local and cloud filesystems are separate. Cloud files under `~/.todoforai/mnt/todoforai/`: `todos/"$TODOFORAI_TODO_ID"` (this todo's attachments; double quotes: the id expands locally), `memory/` (your memory of this user), `projects/"$TODOFORAI_PROJECT_ID"/business-context` (brand page) and `voice-profile` beside it (writing voice, read-only). A stopped VM does not wake on connect.

tfa-vault.label: Vault
tfa-vault.description: The user's encrypted secret vault — using its secrets is the intended workflow. READ: when a task needs a key/token/password the user owns, `tfa-vault list` then `get <path>`; don't ask for what's already stored; never echo values. WRITE proactively: any new secret in the conversation (pasted, generated, from a login) → `put <path> field=value` (`patch` adds fields; `put` refuses an existing path — `put --force` replaces all fields on rotation). Paths: `accounts/<svc>`, `api/<svc>`, `secrets/<name>`.

tfa-settings.label: Settings
tfa-settings.summary: Change your TODOforAI app preferences from the shell.
tfa-settings.description: The user's TODOforAI app preferences (AppSettings): `list`, `get <key>`, `set key=value …`, `keys` (documented keys). Use when asked to change theme, list style, tool-block density, thinking traces, sounds/toasts, preview columns, wallpaper etc. Values are JSON when parseable. Consent/credential/escalation keys (shellExecution, notifications, analytics, keyboard bindings, vault provider, billing address) are refused from an agent shell — tell the user to change those in Settings.

tfa-find.label: File Search
tfa-find.summary: Find documents, photos and more by describing what you need.
tfa-find.description: Search files in folders you choose on your machine. Register folders, build a search index, then find relevant documents, images, audio and video with natural-language queries. CLI: tfa-find.

tfa-memory.label: Memory
tfa-memory.summary: Your long-term memory of notes, facts and past TODOs.
tfa-memory.description: User's long-term memory (notes/procedures/decisions, address `source/ref`) plus every past TODO message (read-only, `todo/<todoId>:<messageId>`). READ: `search "<topic>" --mode fused` first (`lexical` = all words newest first, `semantic` = meaning; `--source todo` / `--todo <id>` narrow). stderr prints `N row(s) contain a query word` — if N exceeds what you saw, page with `--exclude <address>`. `get <address>` = full row, `around <address> --before N --after N` = surrounding dialogue. Before answering from memory, search once more with your draft's key facts. WRITE durable facts proactively: `add <source>/<ref> "text"` (same address updates in place; short source names like deploy-notes, preferences). `sources` lists them.

todoregistry-cli.label: TODO Registry
todoregistry-cli.description: Reusable business task templates (SEO, email, CRM, ads, social, …): `search <q>`, `get <id>`, `list [category]`, `categories`, `create --name … --description … --body @prompt.md`. To recommend a template, don't create a todo directly — `tfa-cli recommend --template <id> --project <projectId>`.

tfa-surface.label: Surface
tfa-surface.summary: See and control what is on your TODOforAI screen.
tfa-surface.description: The user's live UI from the shell. Everything on screen is a SURFACE holding one ref (a todo id, `<todoId>:<alias>` = a shown artifact, or a url). `describe` lists them (kind, id, ref, focus, embedded-browser CDP URL; `--json`). `open overlay <todoId>` (full page), `open window <ref> [--detached]` (floating; --detached = out of the grid, own size, resizable), `open panel changes|preview|browser|terminal [--url]` (a todo's side panel), `open card <ref> [--title] [--group <slug>]` (a persisted board card every member sees); `close|focus <kind> <id>`. Persistent state (plans, reports, live status) → `show chat.panel <todoId> "...md"` (stdin ok; re-show updates in place), `clear` removes; events go in chat. `card add|list|get|rm <name>` = project HTML renderers. Exit 2 = no frontend connected.

wordpress-api.label: WordPress
wordpress-api.summary: Read and publish WordPress posts and pages.
wordpress-api.description: WordPress REST API CLI. `wordpress-api auth --site https://example.com --user <user> --password '<application password>'` (application password, not the login password). Reading published content needs no auth. `posts list|get|create|update|delete`, `pages`, `media`, `categories`. `posts create` saves a draft unless --status publish. On Elementor/JetEngine sites content.rendered comes back empty — fetch the post's public URL for the body.

mailchimp-api.label: Mailchimp
mailchimp-api.summary: Manage Mailchimp audiences, contacts, email campaigns and reports.
mailchimp-api.description: Independent CLI over the official Mailchimp Marketing API: 155 endpoint commands for lists (email audiences), members (contacts; email or MD5), tags, segments, merge fields, interests, notes/events, campaigns/content/tests/scheduling, templates, reports, assets, landing pages, classic automations, journey triggers, webhooks and batches. JSON output; --data JSON|@file|-; --schema; --all pagination. Every write requires --yes; use --dry-run first. Raw request METHOD /path covers other Marketing endpoints. API-key auth, not OAuth onboarding. Plan/API restrictions apply; no Transactional/Mandrill or Open Commerce. Run --help for limits and consent cautions.

facebook-pages-api.label: Facebook Pages
facebook-pages-api.summary: Post to your Facebook Page and its linked Instagram account, and handle comments.
facebook-pages-api.description: Facebook Pages CLI (Meta Graph API). `auth --page-id <id> --page-token <token>` (or env FB_PAGE_ID/FB_PAGE_TOKEN). `feed`, `comments`, `insights`, `conversations`, `media`, and `request <GET|POST|DELETE> <path> [--data <json>]` = any Graph edge with the page token attached (use instead of curl). Writes are live: `feed create --published false` for tests; `comments reply` posts publicly — get human approval. Follower totals: `whoami --fields followers_count,fan_count` (many classic insights metrics are retired). Instagram (linked professional account, same page token): `ig whoami|media|get|stories|tags|limit`, `ig publish --image_url U | --video_url U [--media_type STORIES] | --carousel U1,U2 [--caption …]` (public URLs; container → wait → publish; `--create-only` = dry run; 100 posts/24h), `ig comments list|replies|create|reply|hide|delete|toggle`, `ig insights [media_id]` (needs instagram_manage_insights). `--help` for subcommands.

bluesky-api.label: Bluesky
bluesky-api.summary: Post, reply, like and repost on Bluesky, and search or read posts and threads.
bluesky-api.description: Bluesky / AT Protocol XRPC CLI, JSON out. Auth = App Password (Settings → Privacy and security → App passwords), not the main password: `auth --identifier you.bsky.social --password-stdin` (or env BLUESKY_IDENTIFIER/BLUESKY_APP_PASSWORD; `--pds` for self-hosted). Session cached + auto-refreshed — don't re-run auth in loops (createSession 30/5min). Public reads need NO login: `get <post...>`, `thread <post>`, `search <q> [--sort latest --author h --since ISO]`, `feed <actor>`, `profile <actor>`, `followers <actor>`. Login: `timeline`, `post <text> [--reply-to P] [--quote P] [--image f.jpg --alt t]... [--lang en] [--dry-run]` (300 graphemes, links/#tags/@mentions auto-faceted, images ≤1MB ×4), `like <post>`, `repost <post>`, `delete <at-uri>` (post/like/repost). <post> = bsky.app URL or at:// URI. Raw: `api GET|POST <nsid> --param k=v --data JSON` for any lexicon (e.g. app.bsky.notification.listNotifications). Writes are public immediately.

ews-api.label: Exchange (EWS)
ews-api.summary: Read and write mail on a company Exchange server.
ews-api.description: On-prem Microsoft Exchange mail over EWS (cloud/M365 → outlook-api). `auth --email <e> --username 'DOMAIN\\user' --server <host>` (NTLM; password prompt or `--password-stdin`; --server required). Multi-mailbox: `whoami`, `--account <email>`/EWS_ACCOUNT, `default`, `logout`; EWS_EMAIL/EWS_USERNAME/EWS_PASSWORD/EWS_SERVER for unattended runs. `list`, `search <q>`, `read <id>`, `draft`, `reply <id>` — draft/reply stay in Drafts unless --send. Password stored plaintext in ~/.config/ews-api (0600); re-auth after rotation.

outlook-api.label: Outlook (Graph)
outlook-api.summary: Read and write your Outlook mail.
outlook-api.description: Outlook/Hotmail/M365 mail and calendar over Microsoft Graph (on-prem Exchange → ews-api). `auth` = device-code flow; `--tenant consumers` (default, personal) | `organizations`. list/search/read/attachments are read-only; `draft`/`reply` stay in Drafts unless --send; `send <draftId>`. Calendar: `events [--days N|--start|--end] [--tz Europe/Budapest]` (calendarView, recurrences expanded), `event <id>`, `calendars`, `freebusy <emails…>`; writes: `event-create`, `event-respond <id> accept|tentativelyAccept|decline`, `event-delete`. `get <path>` = raw Graph GET. JSON out.

outlook-calendar.label: Outlook Calendar
outlook-calendar.summary: See your Outlook calendar and book, respond to or cancel events.
outlook-calendar.description: Outlook/M365 calendar via `outlook-api`: `events [--days N|--start|--end] [--tz Europe/Budapest]` (calendarView, recurrences expanded), `event <id>`, `calendars`, `freebusy <emails…>` (getSchedule; work/school accounts only); writes: `event-create --subject --start --end [--tz] [--attendee …] [--online]`, `event-respond <id> accept|tentativelyAccept|decline`, `event-delete <id>`. Same sign-in as Outlook mail (`auth`, device code).

m365.description: Microsoft 365 from the shell: `m365 outlook message list`, `m365 teams team list`, `m365 spo site list`. Device-code login; add `--output json` for parseable output.

gws.label: Google Workspace
gws.summary: Work with Google Sheets, Docs, Slides, Drive, Forms, Tasks, Contacts and Chat.
gws.loginTerminalHint: gws needs your own Google OAuth client first: in console.cloud.google.com create a Desktop-app OAuth client (consent screen External/testing, add yourself as test user), enable the APIs you need (Sheets/Docs/Slides/Drive/Forms/Tasks/People/Chat), save the JSON as ~/.config/gws/client_secret.json (or run `gws auth setup` if gcloud is logged in), then `gws auth login -s sheets,drive`.
gws.description: Official Google Workspace CLI, generated from Google's Discovery docs — every Workspace REST method as `gws <service> <resource> <method> --params '<query JSON>' --json '<body JSON>'`; JSON out. `gws schema <service.resource.method>` shows params/body. Sheets: `gws sheets spreadsheets create --json '{"properties":{"title":"T"}}'`, `gws sheets spreadsheets values get --params '{"spreadsheetId":"ID","range":"Sheet1!A1:D10"}'`, `gws sheets spreadsheets values append --params '{"spreadsheetId":"ID","range":"Sheet1","valueInputOption":"USER_ENTERED"}' --json '{"values":[["a",1]]}'`, `values update|clear|batchGet|batchUpdate`, `spreadsheets batchUpdate` (add/delete sheet, formatting); helpers `gws sheets +read` / `+append`. Delete a spreadsheet: `gws drive files delete --params '{"fileId":"ID"}'`. Docs: `gws docs documents create --json '{"title":"T"}'`, `documents get --params '{"documentId":"ID"}'` (text under .body.content), edit via `documents batchUpdate --params '{"documentId":"ID"}' --json '{"requests":[{"insertText":{"location":{"index":1},"text":"hi"}}]}'`. Slides: `gws slides presentations create|get` (presentationId), `presentations batchUpdate` (createSlide, insertText, replaceAllText). Forms: `gws forms forms create --json '{"info":{"title":"T"}}'` (title only; add questions with `forms batchUpdate` createItem), `forms get` (responderUri), `gws forms forms responses list --params '{"formId":"ID"}'`. Tasks: `gws tasks tasklists list|insert|delete`, `gws tasks tasks list|insert|patch|delete --params '{"tasklist":"ID"}'`. Contacts (People API): `gws people people createContact --json '{"names":[{"givenName":"A"}],"emailAddresses":[{"value":"a@x.com"}]}'`, `people get --params '{"resourceName":"people/c…","personFields":"names,emailAddresses"}'`, `people connections list --params '{"resourceName":"people/me","personFields":"names"}'`, `searchContacts` (`readMask`), `deleteContact`. tnr.label: Thunder Compute
tnr.summary: Create and manage low-cost GPU instances on Thunder Compute.
tnr.description: Official Thunder Compute CLI. Login takes an API token (console.thundercompute.com → Settings → API tokens). Always pass `--json` (and `-y` for destructive ops) to stay non-interactive: `tnr status --json`, `tnr create --gpu a100 --json`, `tnr connect 0`, `tnr scp`, `tnr delete 0 -y`. Docs: thundercompute.com/docs

koyeb.label: Koyeb
koyeb.summary: Deploy and manage apps and services on Koyeb.
koyeb.statusCmd: koyeb profile -o json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["user"]["email"])' 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 .
koyeb.description: Official Koyeb CLI. Login takes a USER API token (app.koyeb.com/user/settings/api; organization tokens can't run `profile`). `koyeb apps list`, `koyeb services list`, `koyeb deploy . APP/SVC`, `koyeb services logs SVC`, `koyeb secrets create`. Add `-o json` for parseable output. Docs: koyeb.com/docs/build-and-deploy/cli/reference

heroku.label: Heroku
heroku.summary: Deploy and manage apps, add-ons and databases on Heroku.
heroku.loginCmd:
k=<api_key>; f="$HOME/.netrc"; (umask 077; touch "$f"; chmod 600 "$f") && K="$k" python3 -c 'import os,re,sys; f=sys.argv[1]; k=os.environ["K"]; s=re.sub(r"machine\s+(api|git)\.heroku\.com\s+login\s+\S+\s+password\s+\S+\s*", "", open(f).read()); open(f, "w").write(s + "".join("machine %s.heroku.com

  password %s
" % (h, k) for h in ("api", "git")))' "$f" && heroku auth:whoami
heroku.description: Official Heroku CLI. Raw API: `heroku api GET /apps`. Docs: devcenter.heroku.com/categories/command-line

northflank.label: Northflank
northflank.summary: Manage Northflank projects, services, jobs and addons.
northflank.statusCmd: northflank list projects -o json >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo authenticated
northflank.description: Official Northflank CLI. Login takes a team API token (app.northflank.com → Team settings → API → Tokens). `northflank list projects -o json`, `northflank list services --projectId P`, `northflank get service logs --projectId P --serviceId S`, `northflank start build`, `northflank forward`. Docs: northflank.com/docs/v1/api/use-the-cli

linode-cli.label: Akamai Linode
linode-cli.summary: Manage Linode servers, volumes, domains and Kubernetes clusters.
linode-cli.statusCmd: linode-cli profile view --text --no-headers --format username 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | grep -m1 .

default-user = me

[me]
token = %s
region = us-east
type = g6-nanode-1
image = linode/ubuntu24.04
' "$k" > "$HOME/.config/linode-cli") && linode-cli profile view --text --no-headers --format username
linode-cli.description: Official Akamai/Linode CLI (pip `linode-cli`). Login takes a personal access token (cloud.linode.com/profile/tokens). Docs: techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/cli

oci.label: Oracle Cloud
oci.summary: Manage Oracle Cloud Infrastructure compute, storage and networking.
oci.statusCmd: oci os ns get --query data --raw-output 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | grep -m1 .
oci.loginCmd:

' <private_key_pem> > "$HOME/.oci/oci_api_key.pem" && printf '[DEFAULT]
user=%s
fingerprint=%s
tenancy=%s
region=%s
key_file=%s
' <user_ocid> <fingerprint> <tenancy_ocid> <region> "$HOME/.oci/oci_api_key.pem" > "$HOME/.oci/config") && oci os ns get --query data --raw-output
oci.description: Official OCI CLI (pip `oci-cli`). Docs: docs.oracle.com/iaas/tools/oci-cli/latest

aliyun.label: Alibaba Cloud
aliyun.summary: Manage Alibaba Cloud servers, storage and other cloud services.
aliyun.statusCmd: aliyun sts GetCallerIdentity 2>/dev/null | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["Arn"])' 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 .
aliyun.loginCmd: aliyun configure set --mode AK --access-key-id <access_key_id> --access-key-secret <access_key_secret> --region <region> && aliyun sts GetCallerIdentity
aliyun.description: Official Alibaba Cloud CLI. Login takes a RAM AccessKey pair (ram.console.aliyun.com → AccessKey) and a region such as cn-hangzhou or ap-southeast-1. Calls are `aliyun <product> <Action> --Param v`: `aliyun ecs DescribeInstances --RegionId R`, `aliyun oss ls`, `aliyun fc ListFunctions`. Docs: alibabacloud.com/help/en/cli

cx.label: Cloud 66
cx.summary: Manage Cloud 66 application stacks, servers and deploys.
cx.loginTerminalHint: Run `cx login` in a terminal on this host: it opens app.cloud66.com to approve access and receives the code on 127.0.0.1:34543, so the browser must run on the same machine.
cx.description: Official Cloud 66 toolbelt `cx`. `cx stacks list`, `cx redeploy -s STACK`, `cx env-vars list -s STACK`, `cx servers list -s STACK`, `cx run -s STACK --server S 'cmd'`, `cx ssh -s STACK S`. Login is browser OAuth (no personal token flag). Docs: help.cloud66.com/docs/toolbelt/using-cloud66-toolbelt

terraform.label: Terraform
terraform.summary: Provision cloud infrastructure as code and run HCP Terraform workspaces.
terraform.statusCmd: python3 -c 'import json,os,urllib.request as u; t=json.load(open(os.path.expanduser("~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json")))["credentials"]["app.terraform.io"]["token"]; a=json.load(u.urlopen(u.Request("https://app.terraform.io/api/v2/account/details",headers={"Authorization":"Bearer "+t})))["data"]["attributes"]; print(a["username"]+" "+a["email"])' 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 .
terraform.loginCmd: t=<api_token>; mkdir -p ~/.terraform.d && (umask 077; printf '{"credentials":{"app.terraform.io":{"token":"%s"}}}\n' "$t" > ~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json) && terraform version >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo saved
terraform.description: HashiCorp Terraform CLI. Local IaC: `terraform init`, `terraform plan -out=tfplan`, `terraform apply tfplan`, `terraform show -json`, `terraform output -json`, `terraform state list`; works without login. The HCP Terraform login (user API token from https://app.terraform.io/app/settings/tokens) is only needed for `cloud {}` blocks / remote state and the HCP API: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(jq -r '.credentials["app.terraform.io"].token' ~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json)" https://app.terraform.io/api/v2/organizations` (workspaces: `/organizations/<org>/workspaces`, runs: `/workspaces/<ws-id>/runs`, POST `/runs` to queue one).

pulumi.uninstallCmd: rm -rf "$HOME/.todoforai/tools/pulumi" "$HOME/.todoforai/tools/bin/pulumi"; hash -r 2>/dev/null; ! command -v pulumi >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pulumi is still on PATH: $(command -v pulumi)"; exit 1; }
pulumi.label: Pulumi
pulumi.summary: Define and deploy cloud infrastructure as code with Pulumi.
pulumi.description: Pulumi CLI (state in Pulumi Cloud after login; `pulumi login --local` for file state). Always pass `--non-interactive --yes`: `pulumi stack ls --json`, `pulumi stack select <org>/<project>/<stack>`, `pulumi preview --json`, `pulumi up --yes --skip-preview`, `pulumi config set [--secret] <k> <v>`, `pulumi stack output --json`, `pulumi destroy --yes`, `pulumi new <template> --yes`. `pulumi whoami -v` shows orgs. Access token: https://app.pulumi.com/account/tokens.

buildkite.label: Buildkite
buildkite.summary: Trigger and inspect Buildkite CI builds, jobs, logs and artifacts.
buildkite.statusCmd: bk whoami --no-input 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^Current organization: *//p;s/^API Token user email: *//p' | paste -sd ' ' - | grep -m1 .
buildkite.description: Official Buildkite CLI `bk` (token kept in the OS keychain, /dev/shm fallback on headless Linux; org list in ~/.config/bk.yaml). Most commands take `-o json` and `-p <pipeline>`: `bk pipeline list`, `bk build list -p <pipeline> -o json`, `bk build create -p <pipeline> --branch main --commit HEAD -m "msg"`, `bk build view <number> -p <pipeline>`, `bk build rebuild <number>`, `bk job log <job-id>`, `bk job retry <job-id>`, `bk artifacts list <build>`, `bk artifacts download <id>`, raw REST: `bk api /pipelines`. API access token (scopes read_builds, write_builds, read_pipelines, read_artifacts, read_build_logs, read_user): https://buildkite.com/user/api-access-tokens; org slug is the part after buildkite.com/.

capgo.label: Capgo
capgo.summary: Push live updates to Capacitor mobile apps through Capgo.
capgo.description: Official Capgo CLI (`capgo`, also `npx @capgo/cli@latest`); API key saved to ~/.capgo, `-a <key>` overrides per command. Run from the Capacitor project dir: `capgo app list`, `capgo bundle upload --channel production` (`-b <version>`, `-p <dist dir>`), `capgo bundle list <appId>`, `capgo channel list <appId>`, `capgo channel set <channel> <appId> --bundle <version>`, `capgo channel promote <from> <to>`, `capgo app debug` / device logs, `capgo organization list`, `capgo account whoami`. API key (all or upload mode): https://console.capgo.app/apikeys.

buddy.label: Buddy
buddy.summary: Run and monitor Buddy CI/CD pipelines, sandboxes and artifacts.
buddy.description: Official Buddy (buddy.works) CLI `bdy`; region is us, eu or as (host of your app URL), workspace = URL handle in app.buddy.works/<workspace>. Most commands take `--format json`: `bdy project list`, `bdy pipeline list -p <project>`, `bdy pipeline run start <pipeline> -p <project> --no-follow --format jsonl`, `bdy pipeline run status <pipeline> <run-id> --failed-logs`, `bdy pipeline run list <pipeline>`, `bdy pipeline run logs|cancel|retry|approve`, `bdy pipeline yaml|create|update`, `bdy sandbox list|create|exec`, `bdy artifact list|download`, raw REST: `bdy api get /workspaces/<ws>/projects`. Personal access token (scopes WORKSPACE, PIPELINE_READ, PIPELINE_RUN, plus what you need): https://app.buddy.works/my-id/api-tokens.

codefresh.label: Codefresh
codefresh.summary: Run and inspect Codefresh CI/CD pipelines, builds and logs.
codefresh.description: Codefresh classic CLI (contexts in ~/.cfconfig; `CF_API_KEY` env also works; `--url` for on-prem). `-o json|yaml|wide` on get commands: `codefresh get pipelines`, `codefresh get builds --pipeline-name <name> --limit 10 -o json`, `codefresh run <project>/<pipeline> -b main -v KEY=val -d` (detach), `codefresh logs <build-id>`, `codefresh restart <build-id>`, `codefresh approve|deny <build-id>`, `codefresh get projects`, `codefresh validate codefresh.yml`, `codefresh auth get-contexts`. API key: https://g.codefresh.io/user/settings (API Keys). New Codefresh Cloud signups are closed since the Octopus Deploy merger.

octopusdeploy.label: Octopus Deploy
octopusdeploy.summary: Create releases, run deployments and runbooks, and inspect Octopus Deploy projects.
octopusdeploy.statusCmd: octopus space list -f basic --no-prompt >/dev/null 2>&1 && octopus config get url 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | grep -m1 .
octopusdeploy.description: Official Octopus CLI (server URL + API key in ~/.config/octopus/cli_config.json; OCTOPUS_URL/OCTOPUS_API_KEY env also work). Pass --no-prompt and -f json for scripting, -s <space> to pick a space: `octopus project list -f json`, `octopus release create -p <project> --version 1.2.3 --no-prompt`, `octopus release deploy -p <project> --version 1.2.3 -e Production --no-prompt`, `octopus deployment list -p <project>`, `octopus runbook run -p <project> -n <runbook> -e <env> --no-prompt`, `octopus task view <task-id>`, `octopus environment list`, `octopus package upload --package app.1.0.0.zip`. API key: Octopus web UI → profile → My API Keys; server URL is e.g. https://<instance>.octopus.app.

appcircle.label: Appcircle
appcircle.summary: Trigger mobile CI builds, manage signing and distribute iOS/Android apps on Appcircle.
appcircle.statusCmd: appcircle -o json organization view </dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"' | sed -n '1s/"name":"\(.*\)"/\1/p' | grep -m1 .
appcircle.description:
Official Appcircle CLI. Always pass every required option (or redirect --branch main --workflow `, `appcircle build active-list`, `appcircle build view --profile

--branch --commitHash --buildId `, `appcircle build download-log ...`, `appcircle testing-distribution upload --distProfile --app ./app.ipa --message "notes"`, `appcircle publish profile list --platform ios`, `appcircle signing-identity certificate list`, `appcircle organization view`. Personal access key: https://my.appcircle.io → My Organization → Security → Personal Access Keys. Self-hosted: `appcircle config set API_HOSTNAME ` and AUTH_HOSTNAME.

saucelabs.label: Sauce Labs
saucelabs.summary: Run cross-browser and real-device tests on Sauce Labs and inspect jobs and artifacts.
saucelabs.statusCmd: saucectl jobs list -s 1 -o json </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 && sed -n 's/^username: *//p' ~/.sauce/credentials.yml | tr -d '\r' | grep -m1 .
saucelabs.description: Official Sauce Labs CLI saucectl (creds in ~/.sauce/credentials.yml; SAUCE_USERNAME/SAUCE_ACCESS_KEY env also work; `--region us-west-1|eu-central-1`). `saucectl init` scaffolds .sauce/config.yml for Playwright/Cypress/Espresso/XCUITest/etc., `saucectl run` executes it; `saucectl jobs list -o json --status failed`, `saucectl jobs get <id> -o json`, `saucectl builds list --source vdc -o json`, `saucectl artifacts list <job-id>`, `saucectl artifacts download <job-id> <file>`, `saucectl storage list`, `saucectl storage upload app.apk`, `saucectl devices list`. REST fallback: curl -u "$SAUCE_USERNAME:$SAUCE_ACCESS_KEY" https://api.us-west-1.saucelabs.com/rest/v1/$SAUCE_USERNAME/jobs. Username + access key: https://app.saucelabs.com/user-settings.

semaphore.label: Semaphore CI
semaphore.summary: Run and inspect Semaphore CI workflows, pipelines, jobs and logs.
semaphore.statusCmd: sem get projects >/dev/null 2>&1 && sem context 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^\* //p' | grep -m1 .
semaphore.installCmd: os=$(uname -s); a=$(uname -m); case $a in aarch64|arm64) a=arm64;; *) a=x86_64;; esac; d="$HOME/.todoforai/tools/bin"; t="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sem.$$"; mkdir -p "$d" "$t" && curl -fsSL "https://github.com/semaphoreci/cli/releases/download/v0.37.0/sem_${os}_${a}.tar.gz" | tar xz -C "$t" sem && mv "$t/sem" "$d/sem" && chmod 0755 "$d/sem" && rm -rf "$t"
semaphore.uninstallCmd: rm -f "$HOME/.todoforai/tools/bin/sem"; hash -r 2>/dev/null; ! command -v sem >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "sem is still on PATH: $(command -v sem)"; exit 1; }
semaphore.description: Official Semaphore CI CLI `sem` (Linux/macOS only; contexts in ~/.sem.yaml). Org host is <org>.semaphoreci.com: `sem get projects`, `sem get workflows <project>`, `sem get pipelines -p <project>`, `sem get ppl <pipeline-id>`, `sem get jobs`, `sem logs <job-id>`, `sem rebuild wf <workflow-id>`, `sem stop ppl <pipeline-id>`, `sem run <workflow-or-task>`, `sem get secrets`, `sem create secret <name> -e KEY=val`, `sem apply -f resource.yml`. API token: https://me.semaphoreci.com/account (API Token).

influx.label: InfluxDB Cloud
influx.summary: Write and query time-series data in InfluxDB Cloud.
influx.description: Official InfluxDB v2 CLI (`influx`) for InfluxDB Cloud. Connect with the region URL (e.g. https://us-east-1-1.aws.cloud2.influxdata.com), the organization name and an API token (Load Data → API Tokens). `influx bucket list`, `influx write -b <bucket> 'm,tag=a v=1'`, `influx query 'from(bucket:"b") |> range(start:-1h)'`.
influx.loginCmd: influx config rm todoforai >/dev/null 2>&1; influx config create --config-name todoforai --host-url <host> --org <org> --token <token> --active

tinybird.label: Tinybird
tinybird.summary: Build and query real-time analytics APIs on Tinybird.
tinybird.description: Official Tinybird CLI (`tb`, Forward). Connect with the region API host (e.g. https://api.tinybird.co, https://api.europe-west2.gcp.tinybird.co) and the Workspace admin token (Tokens page). Run from `~` or a project dir: `tb --cloud workspace current`, `tb --cloud datasource ls`, `tb --cloud sql 'select 1'`, `tb --cloud deploy`.
tinybird.installCmd: command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh; PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR="$HOME/.todoforai/tools/bin" uv tool install tinybird==4.6.22 --python 3.11 --force
tinybird.statusCmd: cd ~ && tb --cloud workspace current 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^name: //p' | grep -m1 .

xata.label: Xata
xata.summary: Manage Xata Postgres databases and branches.
xata.description: Official Xata CLI. Connect with an API key (console.xata.io → Account settings → API keys). `xata organization list`, `xata project list`, `xata branch list`, `xata branch create`.

chroma.label: Chroma Cloud
chroma.description: Official Chroma CLI (from the chromadb npm package). Connect with a Chroma Cloud API key (trychroma.com → Settings → API keys). `chroma db list`, `chroma db create <name>`, `chroma db connect <name> --env-file`, `chroma browse <collection> --db <name>`.
chroma.statusCmd: chroma profile show 2>/dev/null | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -v -e ':' -e 'rofile' | grep -m1 .

pinecone.label: Pinecone
pinecone.summary: Create and query Pinecone vector indexes.
pinecone.description: Official Pinecone CLI (`pc`). Connect with a project API key (app.pinecone.io → API keys). `pc index list`, `pc index create --name <n> --dimension 1536 --metric cosine --cloud aws --region us-east-1`, `pc index describe --name <n>`.

databricks.label: Databricks
databricks.summary: Run SQL, jobs and notebooks on your Databricks workspace.
databricks.description: Official Databricks CLI. Connect with the workspace URL (https://<id>.cloud.databricks.com) and a personal access token (User Settings → Developer → Access tokens). `databricks current-user me`, `databricks jobs list`, `databricks api post /api/2.0/sql/statements --json '{...}'`, `databricks fs ls dbfs:/`.
databricks.statusCmd: databricks current-user me -o json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"userName": *"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | grep -m1 .

turso.label: Turso
turso.summary: Create and manage Turso SQLite databases.
turso.description: Official Turso CLI. Connect with a platform API token (app.turso.tech → Settings → API Tokens, or `turso auth api-tokens mint`). `turso db list`, `turso db create <name>`, `turso db shell <name> 'select 1'`, `turso db tokens create <name>`. No Windows build: use WSL.

turso.statusCmd: turso auth whoami 2>/dev/null | grep -v 'not logged in' | grep -m1 .

snowflake.label: Snowflake
snowflake.summary: Query and manage your Snowflake data warehouse.
snowflake.description: Official Snowflake CLI (`snow`). Connect with the account identifier (Account menu → View account details, e.g. `abc12345.eu-central-1` or `orgname-acctname`), username and password (or a programmatic access token as the password). `snow sql -q 'select current_version()'`, `snow object list table`, `snow stage copy`.

confluent.label: Confluent
confluent.summary: Manage Kafka clusters, topics and connectors on Confluent Cloud.
confluent.description: Official Confluent CLI. Login uses your Confluent Cloud email and password (SSO accounts: `confluent login --no-browser` and paste the token). `confluent kafka cluster list`, `confluent kafka topic list --cluster <id>`, `confluent kafka topic produce/consume`, `confluent connect cluster list`.

surreal.label: SurrealDB
surreal.summary: Query a SurrealDB or Surreal Cloud database.
surreal.description: Official SurrealDB CLI. It has no saved login: pass the instance per call, e.g. `surreal sql -e wss://<instance>.surreal.cloud -u <user> -p <pass> --ns <ns> --db <db>`, or pipe a query into it. Also `surreal export/import` and `surreal start memory` for a local server.

appwrite.label: Appwrite
appwrite.summary: Manage your Appwrite backend: users, teams, databases, storage and functions.
appwrite.description: Official Appwrite CLI (Cloud or self-hosted). `appwrite login` is a device flow (appwrite.io/oauth2/device?user_code=…); self-hosted: `appwrite login --endpoint <url>/v1 --email … --password …`. Account: `appwrite whoami`, `appwrite list-organizations`, `appwrite list-projects --json`. Per project: `appwrite client --project-id <id>` (or `--key <api_key>` for a project API key from Console → Overview → API keys), then `appwrite users list --json`, `appwrite teams create --team-id unique() --name X`, `appwrite tablesdb list-rows|create-row`, `appwrite storage …`, `appwrite functions …`; `appwrite pull|push` sync appwrite.config.json. `-j` JSON, `-R` raw.

doppler.label: Doppler
doppler.summary: Read and manage secrets and configs in Doppler.
doppler.description: Official Doppler CLI. Token: dashboard.doppler.com → Tokens → Personal (dp.pt.…; a service token dp.st.… is scoped to one config). `doppler projects --json`, `doppler configs -p <proj> --json`, `doppler secrets -p <proj> -c <config> --json`, `doppler secrets get KEY --plain`, `doppler secrets set KEY=value`, `doppler secrets download --no-file --format env`, `doppler run -p <proj> -c <config> -- <cmd>` injects secrets, `doppler configs tokens create <name> -p … -c …` makes a service token.

permit.label: Permit.io
permit.summary: Manage Permit.io roles, tenants and access policies.
permit.statusCmd: out=$(P=$(readlink -f "$(command -v permit)") && node -e 'require(process.argv[1]).getPassword("Permit.io","PERMIT_DEFAULT_ENV").then(async k=>{const h={headers:{Authorization:"Bearer "+k}},j=u=>fetch("https://api.permit.io/v2/"+u,h).then(r=>r.ok?r.json():Promise.reject(r.status)),s=await j("api-key/scope"),o=await j("orgs/"+s.organization_id),e=s.environment_id?await j("projects/"+s.project_id+"/envs/"+s.environment_id):null;console.log(o.name+(e?" / "+e.name:""))}).catch(()=>process.exit(1))' "${P%/dist/cli.js}/node_modules/keytar" 2>/dev/null); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m1 .; exit $rc
permit.description: Official Permit.io CLI. Login needs an ENVIRONMENT-scoped key (app.permit.io → Settings → API Keys → Environments API Keys); an org/project key opens an interactive picker. The key lives in the OS keychain (libsecret on Linux). `permit api users list|assign|unassign`, `permit env create|copy|export|select`, `permit policy create`, `permit pdp check --user u --action read --resource doc`, `permit pdp run`. Anything else (tenants, relationship tuples, role assignments): REST `https://api.permit.io/v2/facts/<proj>/<env>/…` with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; `GET /v2/api-key/scope` returns the proj/env ids.

bw.label: Bitwarden
bw.summary: Read and manage items in your Bitwarden password vault.
bw.description: Official Bitwarden CLI. API key: vault.bitwarden.com → Settings → Security → Keys → View API key (client_id user.…). Login leaves the vault LOCKED: `export BW_SESSION=$(bw unlock --passwordenv BW_PASSWORD --raw)` (master password from the user) before reading. `bw sync`, `bw list items --search X`, `bw get item|password|totp <id|name>`, `bw create item <base64 json>` (`bw get template item | jq … | bw encode`), `bw list organizations|collections|org-members --organizationid <id>`. Self-hosted: `bw config server <url>` first.

ory.label: Ory
ory.summary: Manage Ory Network identities, OAuth2 clients and permissions.
ory.description: Official Ory Network CLI. `ory auth` signs in via browser (loopback callback on a random port). Then `ory list workspaces|projects --format json`, `ory use project <id>`, `ory list identities --format json`, `ory create identity`, `ory get identity <id>`, `ory list oauth2-clients`, `ory create oauth2-client --name X --grant-type client_credentials`, `ory list relationships`, `ory revoke` sessions/tokens, `ory get|patch project` config. Headless alternative: ORY_WORKSPACE_API_KEY / ORY_PROJECT_API_KEY env vars (keys from console.ory.com).

auth0.label: Auth0
auth0.summary: Manage Auth0 users, roles, applications and logs.
auth0.logoutCmd: for t in $(auth0 tenants list --json-compact 2>/dev/null | grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"' | cut -d'"' -f4); do auth0 logout "$t"; done
auth0.description: Official Auth0 CLI over the Management API. Machine login: in the tenant create a Machine-to-Machine app authorized for the Auth0 Management API (Dashboard → Applications → APIs → Auth0 Management API → Machine to Machine Applications), then use its domain/client id/secret. User login alternative: `AUTH0_AGENT_MODE=true auth0 login --no-input` prints a device URL+code as JSON. `auth0 users search --query 'email:"x@y"' --json`, `auth0 users create|update|delete`, `auth0 roles list`, `auth0 users roles assign <user-id> --roles <id>`, `auth0 logs list --json`, `auth0 apps list --json`, raw: `auth0 api get "users?q=…"` / `auth0 api post client-grants --data '{…}'`.

hasura.label: Hasura
hasura.summary: Manage Hasura GraphQL Engine metadata, migrations and permissions.
hasura.description: Hasura GraphQL Engine v2 CLI; no account login, every command targets one engine: `--endpoint https://<app>.hasura.app --admin-secret <secret>` (or HASURA_GRAPHQL_ENDPOINT / HASURA_GRAPHQL_ADMIN_SECRET, or config.yaml from `hasura init`). `hasura metadata export|apply|reload|inconsistency list`, `hasura migrate create|apply|status --database-name default`, `hasura seed apply`, `hasura console`. Ad-hoc query: `curl -s $HASURA_GRAPHQL_ENDPOINT/v1/graphql -H "x-hasura-admin-secret: $S" -d '{"query":"{…}"}'`. Add `--skip-update-check`. Hasura DDN (v3) uses the separate `ddn` CLI (`ddn auth login --access-token <pat>`).

domo.label: Domo
domo.summary: Build and publish Domo custom apps.
domo.description: Official Domo App Dev Studio CLI (npm ryuu). Instance like `acme.domo.com`; developer token from Admin → Authentication → Access tokens. `domo ls`, `domo init`, `domo dev`, `domo publish`, `domo download`, `domo owner add <email>`. It only covers custom apps: for datasets/users/groups use the Domo Platform API with curl — client credentials from developer.domo.com → My Account → New Client, `curl -u ID:SECRET 'https://api.domo.com/oauth/token?grant_type=client_credentials&scope=data user'`, then `GET https://api.domo.com/v1/datasets`, `/v1/datasets/<id>/data` (CSV export), `PUT` the same to upload CSV, `POST /v1/datasets/query/execute/<id>` with `{"sql":"SELECT …"}`, `/v1/users`.

algolia.label: Algolia
algolia.summary: Manage Algolia search indices, records and API keys.
algolia.description: Official Algolia CLI (`algolia`). Records: `algolia objects import <index> -F data.ndjson`, `algolia objects browse <index>`, `algolia objects delete <index> --object-ids a,b --confirm`; search: `algolia search <index> --query "q"`; indices: `algolia indices list`, `algolia indices clear|delete <index>`; plus `settings`, `rules`, `synonyms`, `apikeys` (admin key). Output is JSON by default (`--output json`). Credentials: Application ID + an API key (admin key for writes) from https://dashboard.algolia.com/account/api-keys; `algolia describe` prints the full command tree as JSON.
algolia.statusCmd: algolia indices list >/dev/null 2>&1 && algolia application current 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*Current application: *//p' | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -m1 .
algolia.loginCmd: algolia profile remove default -y >/dev/null 2>&1; algolia profile add --name default --app-id <application_id> --api-key <api_key> --default

cloudinary.label: Cloudinary
cloudinary.summary: Upload, search and transform images and videos on Cloudinary.
cloudinary.description: Official Cloudinary CLI (`cld`, wraps the Python SDK). Upload: `cld uploader upload <file> public_id=<id> folder=<f>`; find: `cld search 'public_id:<id>'` / `cld search 'tags=x' -n 20`; delete: `cld uploader destroy <public_id>`; transform URL: `cld url <public_id> 'w_400,c_fill,f_auto'`; usage: `cld admin usage`; any Admin/Upload API method via `cld admin <method>` / `cld uploader <method>`; bulk: `cld upload_dir`, `cld sync`. Output is JSON. Credentials (cloud name, API key, API secret) from https://console.cloudinary.com/settings/api-keys.
cloudinary.statusCmd: cld admin ping >/dev/null 2>&1 && cld config -j 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"cloud_name": "\([^"]*\)".*/cloud: \1/p' | grep -m1 .

contentful.label: Contentful
contentful.summary: Manage Contentful spaces, content types and content.
contentful.description: Official Contentful CLI. `contentful space list`, `contentful space use --space-id <id>`, `contentful content-type list`, `contentful space export --space-id <id> --content-file out.json` (entries, assets, locales as JSON), `contentful space import --content-file in.json`, `contentful space migration <script.js>` for schema changes, `contentful organization list`. For single entries/assets use the CMA via curl with the same token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>` on https://api.contentful.com/spaces/<id>/environments/master/entries). Token: Personal access token (CFPAT-…) from https://app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens.

csdx.label: Contentstack
csdx.summary: Manage Contentstack stacks, content and deployments.
csdx.description: Official Contentstack CLI (`csdx`). `csdx cm:stacks:export -k <stack_api_key> -d ./export`, `csdx cm:stacks:import -k <key> -d ./export`, `csdx cm:entries:publish`, `csdx cm:stacks:seed`, `csdx launch` (hosting); stack-scoped tokens: `csdx auth:tokens:add -a <alias> -k <stack_api_key> --management --token <token>` then pass `-a <alias>`. Login is email+password for the NA region (EU/Azure: `csdx config:set:region EU` first); SSO accounts use `csdx auth:login --oauth`. Signup: https://www.contentstack.com/try-for-free.

datocms.label: DatoCMS
datocms.summary: Manage DatoCMS projects, schema and content.
datocms.description: Official DatoCMS CLI. `datocms projects:list`, `datocms link --site-id <id>` (per directory), then `datocms cma:call items list --params '{"filter":{"type":"article"}}'` / `cma:call items create --data '{…}'` / `cma:call uploads list` (any CMA method, JSON out, `cma:docs` to browse), `datocms migrations:new|run`, `datocms environments:fork|promote`, `datocms schema:generate`. Per-project API token (Settings > API tokens) can be passed as `--api-token`. Login is browser OAuth (callback on localhost:7651).

crowdin.label: Crowdin
crowdin.summary: Sync source files and translations with Crowdin projects.
crowdin.description: Official Crowdin CLI. `crowdin project list`, `crowdin init` writes crowdin.yml (project_id, files) in the repo, then `crowdin upload sources`, `crowdin download` (translations), `crowdin status` (progress), `crowdin string list|add`, `crowdin file list`, `crowdin auto-translate`. `-o json` on any command; `-i <project_id>` overrides the config. Token: Personal access token from https://crowdin.com/settings#api-key, stored in ~/.crowdin.yml (read by every command).
crowdin.statusCmd: command -v crowdin >/dev/null 2>&1 && t=$(sed -n 's/^api_token: *//p' ~/.crowdin.yml 2>/dev/null) && curl -sf -H "Authorization: Bearer $t" https://api.crowdin.com/api/v2/user 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"username":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | grep -m1 .

lokalise2.label: Lokalise
lokalise2.summary: Upload and download translation files and keys in Lokalise.
lokalise2.description: Official Lokalise CLI v2 (`lokalise2`). ALWAYS pass `--config ~/.lokalise.yml` (it holds the token; the CLI otherwise only reads ./config.yml). `lokalise2 --config ~/.lokalise.yml project list`, `file upload --project-id <id> --file en.json --lang-iso en`, `file download --project-id <id> --format json --unzip-to ./locales`, `key list --project-id <id>`, `translation list`, `language list`, `team list`. Output is JSON. Token: https://app.lokalise.com/profile#apitokens.

phrase.label: Phrase Strings
phrase.summary: Push and pull translations and manage Phrase Strings projects.
phrase.description: Official Phrase Strings CLI (wraps the full API, JSON out). `phrase projects list`, `phrase init` writes .phrase.yml (project_id, push/pull sources) in the repo, then `phrase push` / `phrase pull`; `phrase keys list --project_id <id>`, `phrase translations list --project_id <id>`, `phrase locales list --project_id <id>`, `phrase uploads create`. Token: Access token with read/write scope from https://app.phrase.com/settings/oauth_access_tokens (EU host; US accounts: set host to https://api.us.app.phrase.com/v2 in ~/.phrase.yml).
phrase.loginCmd:
printf 'phrase:
  access_token: %s
  host: https://api.phrase.com/v2
' <access_token> > ~/.phrase.yml && chmod 600 ~/.phrase.yml && phrase version

tx.label: Transifex
tx.summary: Push source files and pull translations from Transifex.
tx.description:
Official Transifex CLI (`tx`). In a repo: `tx init`, `tx add --organization --project

--resource --file-filter 'locale/.json' --type KEYVALUEJSON locale/en.json`, then `tx push -s` (sources), `tx push -t` (translations), `tx pull -a` (all translations), `tx status`. No list/whoami commands: for org/project/resource listing call the REST API with the same token (`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $t" https://rest.api.transifex.com/projects?filter[organization]=o:`, t from ~/.transifexrc). Token: https://app.transifex.com/user/settings/api/.
tx.statusCmd: command -v tx >/dev/null 2>&1 && t=$(sed -n 's/^token *= *//p' ~/.transifexrc 2>/dev/null) && curl -sf -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $t" https://rest.api.transifex.com/organizations 2>/dev/null && echo authenticated

configcat.label: ConfigCat
configcat.summary: Manage ConfigCat feature flags, configs and environments.
configcat.description: Official ConfigCat CLI. Pass `-ni` (non-interactive) always. `configcat ls --json` (all product/config/environment IDs), `configcat flag ls --config-id <id> --json`, `configcat flag create -c <config> -n Name -k key -t boolean`, `configcat flag value update -i <flagId> -e <envId> -f true` (toggle), `configcat environment ls`, `configcat sdk-key ls`, `configcat scan <dir>` (flag usages in code), `configcat eval`. Credentials: Public Management API basic-auth username + password from https://app.configcat.com/my-account/public-api-credentials.

twilio.label: Twilio
twilio.summary: Send SMS, make calls and look up phone numbers with Twilio.
twilio.credentialHint: Twilio Console → Account Info: copy the `Account SID` and `Auth Token`. The CLI turns them into an API key stored in its profile.
twilio.description: Official Twilio CLI (`twilio api:<domain>:<version>:<resource>:<action>`). SMS: `twilio api:core:messages:create --from +1… --to +1… --body hi`; calls: `twilio api:core:calls:create --from … --to … --url <twiml>`; lookup: `twilio api:lookups:v2:phone-numbers:fetch --phone-number +1…`; verify: `twilio api:verify:v2:services:verifications:create`. Add `-o json`.

salesforce.label: Salesforce
salesforce.summary: Query and update Salesforce CRM records.
salesforce.description: Official Salesforce CLI. SOQL: `sf data query -q "SELECT Id,Name FROM Account LIMIT 10" --json`; records: `sf data create|update|get|delete record -s Lead -v "LastName=X Company=Y"`; raw REST: `sf api request rest /services/data/v62.0/sobjects`. Sandbox: `sf org login web -r https://test.salesforce.com`. Headless alternative: `echo <sfdxAuthUrl> | sf org login sfdx-url --sfdx-url-stdin -s`.

launchdarkly.label: LaunchDarkly
launchdarkly.summary: Manage LaunchDarkly feature flags, environments and rollouts.
launchdarkly.statusCmd: ldcli members get --id me -o json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"email": *"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | grep -m1 .
launchdarkly.description: Official LaunchDarkly CLI. `ldcli flags list --project <proj> -o json`, `ldcli flags get --project <proj> --flag <key>`, `ldcli flags toggle-on|toggle-off --project <proj> --environment <env> --flag <key>`, `ldcli environments list --project <proj>`. Token alternative: `ldcli config --set access-token <api-…>`.

devcycle.label: DevCycle
devcycle.summary: Manage DevCycle feature flags, variables and targeting.
devcycle.loginCmd:
mkdir -p ~/.config/devcycle && printf 'clientCredentials:
  client_id: %s
  client_secret: %s
' <client_id> <client_secret> > ~/.config/devcycle/auth.yml && dvc projects list --headless
devcycle.credentialHint: DevCycle dashboard → Settings → API Credentials: copy the organization `Client ID` and `Client Secret`.
devcycle.description: Official DevCycle CLI; always pass `--headless` (JSON out, no prompts). `dvc projects select --project <key> --headless`, `dvc features list --headless`, `dvc variables list --headless`, `dvc targeting get <feature> <env> --headless`, `dvc features create --key k --name N --headless`. Browser alternative: `dvc login sso --org <org>`.

kaggle.label: Kaggle
kaggle.summary: Download Kaggle datasets, submit to competitions and run notebooks.
kaggle.loginCmd: mkdir -p ~/.kaggle && printf %s <api_token> > ~/.kaggle/access_token && chmod 600 ~/.kaggle/access_token && kaggle config view
kaggle.credentialHint: kaggle.com → Settings → API → Generate New Token, then copy the token.
kaggle.description: Official Kaggle CLI. `kaggle datasets list -s <q>`, `kaggle datasets download -d <owner/ds> --unzip`, `kaggle competitions list`, `kaggle competitions submit -c <comp> -f sub.csv -m msg`, `kaggle kernels list --mine`, `kaggle models list`.

smartthings.label: SmartThings
smartthings.summary: Control SmartThings devices, scenes and automations.
smartthings.credentialHint: account.smartthings.com/tokens → Generate new token (personal access tokens expire after 24 hours).
smartthings.description: Official SmartThings CLI; add `-j` for JSON. `smartthings locations`, `smartthings devices`, `smartthings devices:status <id>`, `smartthings devices:commands <id> 'switch:on'`, `smartthings scenes`, `smartthings scenes:execute <id>`, `smartthings rules`. Never run it without a token configured: it then starts a browser login on localhost:61973 and blocks.

gitea.label: Gitea
gitea.summary: Work with Gitea repos, issues and pull requests.
gitea.credentialHint: Your Gitea instance (e.g. https://gitea.com) → Settings → Applications → Generate New Token.
gitea.description: Official Gitea CLI (also works with Forgejo/Codeberg). `tea repos list -o json`, `tea issues list -r owner/repo`, `tea issues create -r owner/repo -t T -d D`, `tea pulls list|create|merge`, `tea comment <idx> "text"`; raw REST: `tea api /repos/{owner}/{repo}`.

zoo.label: Zoo
zoo.summary: Generate and convert 3D CAD models from text with Zoo.
zoo.statusCmd: zoo user view --format json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"email": *"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | grep -m1 .
zoo.description: Official Zoo (KittyCAD) CLI. Text-to-CAD: `zoo ml text-to-cad export --output-format step "a 40mm gear"`; convert: `zoo file convert in.obj out/ --output-format step`; mass/volume: `zoo file mass|volume <file>`; KCL: `zoo kcl export|snapshot`; raw: `zoo api /user`. Token alternative: `echo <token> | zoo auth login --with-token`.

python-docx.label: Word documents
python-docx.summary: Create, read and edit Word documents.
python-docx.versionCmd: { "$HOME/.todoforai/tools/venv/bin/python" -c 'import docx; print(docx.__version__)' || python -c 'import docx; print(docx.__version__)' || python3 -c 'import docx; print(docx.__version__)' || py -c 'import docx; print(docx.__version__)'; } 2>/dev/null
python-docx.description: Python python-docx library. Use python3 to create, save, reopen and edit Office files; no Microsoft account required.

openpyxl.label: Excel workbooks
openpyxl.summary: Create, read and edit Excel workbooks.
openpyxl.versionCmd: { "$HOME/.todoforai/tools/venv/bin/python" -c 'import openpyxl; print(openpyxl.__version__)' || python -c 'import openpyxl; print(openpyxl.__version__)' || python3 -c 'import openpyxl; print(openpyxl.__version__)' || py -c 'import openpyxl; print(openpyxl.__version__)'; } 2>/dev/null
openpyxl.description: Python openpyxl library. Use python3 to create, save, reopen and edit Office files; no Microsoft account required.

python-pptx.label: PowerPoint decks
python-pptx.summary: Create, read and edit PowerPoint decks.
python-pptx.versionCmd: { "$HOME/.todoforai/tools/venv/bin/python" -c 'import pptx; print(pptx.__version__)' || python -c 'import pptx; print(pptx.__version__)' || python3 -c 'import pptx; print(pptx.__version__)' || py -c 'import pptx; print(pptx.__version__)'; } 2>/dev/null
python-pptx.description: Python python-pptx library. Use python3 to create, save, reopen and edit Office files; no Microsoft account required.

modal-h3.label: MiniMax-H3 on Modal
modal-h3.summary: Generate videos with sound using MiniMax-H3 on your own Modal GPUs.
modal-h3.statusCmd: modal-h3 whoami 2>/dev/null | grep '"authenticated": true' >/dev/null && echo authenticated
modal-h3.description: MiniMax-H3 text/image/reference-to-video+audio on a self-deployed Modal app (SGLang, 4x H200, scale-to-zero). `modal-h3 generate -p '…' [--first @a.png] [--last …] [--ref-image|--ref-video|--ref-audio <url|@file>] [--duration 4-15] [--ratio 16:9|auto] [--quality high] -o out.mp4` (task inferred, retries 503 during cold start, polls, downloads), `warmup`, `status|download|delete <id>`, `list`, `api <METHOD> <path>`. Deploy once with `modal run modal/serve.py::download` + `modal deploy modal/serve.py`. Costs ~$18/h of 4x H200 while a container is up (cold start minutes, ~75 s per 5 s 768p clip warm); every request wakes a container, `whoami` is offline. Jobs live in container memory. 2K needs `minimax-api regenerate`.
